newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends at 35.73 in RBI-driven market.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends at 35.73 in RBI-driven market.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.730/735 per dollar on Thursday, compared with 35.72/74 opening, dealers said.
"The market was mostly driven by the RBI (Reserve Bank of India) today," said a dealer at a leading bank. There was no major dollar supply on Thursday.
Dealers reported moderate month-end corporate demand for dollars, but the sentiment was determined by RBI's intervention.
The central bank bought dollars at 35.73 level, they said.
"The spot dollar should trade above the 35.70 level next week," said a dealer. "The (dollar's) downside is limited because of RBI and lack of major supplies," he said.
The forward dollar market was largely steady but premia edged up mildly towards the close on temporary paying pressure.
The six month annualised premium closed at 8.4 percent, up from the previous close of 8.23 percent, dealers said.
"The cost of carrying is almost zero," said a dealer.
Bankers at large are waiting for signs of major dollar purchases by state-run firms in December and repayment of debt.
Some dealers expect bunching of outward remittances to rock the dollar-rupee exchange rate on New Year's eve.
